ai.definition: Mind uploading is the hypothetical process of transferring an individual's consciousness from their biological body into a computer or another artificial host, allowing the mind to exist in a digital form.
ai.howItWorks: Researchers aim to map the intricate neural connections and patterns within the brain, capturing the essential information that defines a person's consciousness. This data would then be used to create a digital replica of the individual's mind, which could potentially operate in virtual or artificial environments.
ai.problemSolved: Mind uploading addresses the issue of physical limitations and mortality by offering a means for consciousness to persist beyond biological death. It also opens up possibilities for enhanced human capabilities through integration with advanced technology.
ai.manufacturing: Current manufacturing processes are theoretical, as no practical method exists yet. However, advancements in neuroscience, nanotechnology, and computer science could eventually enable the creation of such technologies.
ai.buildProcess: The build process would involve developing highly sophisticated brain-computer interfaces (BCIs) capable of non-invasively or minimally invasively reading neural activity. This data would then be processed to create a digital model that can simulate consciousness and behavior.
ai.costDrivers: Key cost drivers include the complexity of the technology, the precision required in mapping neural connections, and the computational power needed to support the digital mind. Additionally, ethical considerations could lead to significant regulatory hurdles and associated costs.
ai.lifecycleOutlook: The outlook is speculative at this stage due to current limitations in technology and understanding of consciousness.
ai.regulation: Regulatory frameworks are non-existent for mind uploading. However, as the technology advances, it will likely face stringent ethical, legal, and safety regulations.
ai.risks: Risks include potential loss of personal identity, privacy concerns, and ethical dilemmas related to the nature of consciousness and personhood. There is also a risk that the digital mind might not accurately replicate human experience or emotions.
ai.profitability: Profitability is uncertain given the speculative nature of the technology and its current state of development. However, if successful, it could revolutionize healthcare, entertainment, and personal computing sectors.
ai.futureDevelopment: Future developments may include improvements in BCIs, advancements in artificial intelligence for simulating consciousness, and breakthroughs in understanding the physical basis of consciousness.

glossary.def: A system that allows direct communication between a human brain and an external device, often used to read neural activity.
The synaptic link between neurons in the brain, which forms the basis of cognitive functions and memory.

subsystems.name: Brain preservation
subsystems.role: stabilise tissue so that synapses remain intact and visible at nanometre resolution.

subsystems.name: High-resolution imaging
subsystems.role: capture every neuron, axon and synapse in a volume of brain tissue.

subsystems.name: Connectome reconstruction
subsystems.role: turn raw images into a complete wiring diagram of the brain.

subsystems.name: Functional inference
subsystems.role: estimate what each connection does — its strength, sign and neurotransmitter.

subsystems.name: Neural simulation
subsystems.role: run the reconstructed network as a living computational model.

subsystems.name: Embodiment and interface
subsystems.role: give the simulated mind senses, a virtual body and a way to act.

buildSteps.title: Preserve the brain
buildSteps.detail: After death, the brain is chemically fixed and stabilised so that fine structures such as synaptic vesicles do not decay.

buildSteps.title: Section and image
buildSteps.detail: The tissue is cut into thousands of ultra-thin slices, each scanned with an electron microscope to reveal membranes and synapses.

buildSteps.title: Align and segment
buildSteps.detail: Slices are stitched into a 3D volume; machine-learning algorithms trace each neuron's branches and mark every synapse.

buildSteps.title: Build the connectome graph
buildSteps.detail: The traced cells and synapses are assembled into a directed graph with cell types, connection strengths and spatial coordinates.

buildSteps.title: Infer functional properties
buildSteps.detail: Molecular and electrical data are used to assign ion channels, receptor types and synaptic weights to each node and edge.

buildSteps.title: Simulate the network
buildSteps.detail: The graph is run on supercomputers using biophysical models that reproduce the electrical behaviour of neurons and synapses.

buildSteps.title: Validate against behaviour
buildSteps.detail: The simulated activity is compared with recordings from the original brain or animal to check that it reproduces known patterns.

buildSteps.title: Provide embodiment and interface
buildSteps.detail: The simulation is connected to virtual senses and actuators so the mind can perceive and act inside a digital environment.

buildSteps.title: Scale to a whole human brain
buildSteps.detail: This step is not yet possible: it would require imaging and simulating roughly 86 billion neurons and their trillions of synapses in real time.

prerequisites.why: Electron microscopy can map small volumes of tissue, but a whole human brain would produce petabytes of data and take decades with current methods.
Machine-learning segmentation is improving, but human proofreading is still needed and does not scale to a human brain.

prerequisites.tech: Understanding of neural coding and consciousness
prerequisites.why: We do not know how patterns of neural activity produce thoughts, memories or subjective experience, so we cannot confirm a simulation is a mind.
Supercomputers exist, but simulating a human brain in real time would need orders of magnitude more compute and storage than we have.
Current methods require slicing the brain, which destroys it; uploading would either kill the original or need a radically new imaging technique.

pathway.milestone: Connectomes of small animals such as the worm and fruit fly have been mapped; human brain maps exist only at the coarse millimetre scale.
pathway.unlocks: Basic understanding of how neural wiring relates to behaviour in simple systems.

pathway.milestone: A complete mouse brain connectome and simulation of simple learned behaviours.
pathway.unlocks: Methods for scaling reconstruction and simulation to mammalian brains.

pathway.milestone: Simulation of a human cortical column or small brain region with realistic input and output.
pathway.unlocks: Proof that detailed human neural circuits can be emulated functionally.

pathway.milestone: Whole human brain emulation with sensory embodiment and validated behaviour.
pathway.unlocks: A candidate digital mind — and urgent ethical questions about identity, consent and rights.
